summary.text: Son of Talaemenes and co-captain of the Maeonians beside Mesthles — a namesake of Antiphus son of Thessalus of Cos, but Homer fixes this man among the Maeonians born beneath Tmolas.

story.text: Homer sets Antiphus beside his brother Mesthles at the head of the Maeonians; their mother was the nymph of the Gygaean lake. Apollodorus names both sons of Talaemenes among the allies who joined the Trojans.
In the rally about Patroclus, Hector heartened Antiphus' brother Mesthles among the captains of the tribes that dwelt round about Troy.
